images.title: Kolam parts make a half
images.purpose: Show that one third of the kolam is 2 sixths, so 1/6 + 1/3 = 3/6, which is one half in lowest terms.
images.composition: One large round kolam on the left with wide margins, and one short sum line on the right.
images.exact_structure: One large plain circle with a grey #6B7280 outline, cut by 3 straight lines through the centre into 6 equal sectors, with no pattern inside. One sector filled teal #0072B2; the next 2 adjacent sectors filled amber #E69F00; the other 3 sectors plain. The 3 filled adjacent sectors form exactly one half of the circle, outlined together by a thicker reddish purple #CC79A7 line. To the right: one sum line. Exactly 1 circle, 6 equal sectors, 1 teal, 2 amber, 3 plain.

images.takeaway: Use the smallest common multiple, add, then give the answer in lowest terms.
images.description: A round kolam in 6 equal sectors: 1 teal sector is 1/6 and 2 amber sectors are 1/3 = 2/6; together the 3 sectors fill half the kolam, so the sum is 3/6 = 1/2.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to trace the purple outline and say what part of the whole kolam it holds.

image_decisions.why: Seeing 3 sixths fill half the kolam makes the lowest terms step obvious.
